adversarial_critique: Claude's coded raw sign (-) and substantive direction (Unfavourable, with exposure oriented as reported) accurately capture Breen and Gillanders's (2024) headline Round 7 finding that regional utilities-sector corruption reduces the probability a household has at least occasional clean water (Access marginal effect = -0.16**, SE = 0.073, N = 44,778 in Table 2 Col 3, PDF p. 10; ordered probit marginal effect on 'Never' lacking clean water = -0.4272**, SE = 0.1860 in Table 3, PDF p. 11). However, Claude extracted only the authors' rounded prose magnitudes (~10% and ~0.5% on PDF p. 10), failed to record the printed marginal effects and region-clustered standard errors (storing SE as 'none, none / clustered by region'), and omitted the lived poverty index control from its covariate list. Substantively, the headline association carries significant multiplicity caveats that Claude omitted: controlling for non-utility regional corruption attenuates the utilities corruption effect to marginal significance (-0.13*, SE = 0.073, p < 0.10 in Table 2 Col 5, PDF pp. 10-11), splitting by infrastructure shows the effect holds only in piped-water areas (-0.14***, SE = 0.045, N = 24,511 in Col 7) and is null in non-piped areas (-0.12, SE = 0.158, N = 20,267 in Col 6), and estimating the model on earlier pre-CAPI Afrobarometer rounds yields a null association in Round 5 and an opposite (positive) association in Round 6 and pooled Rounds 5-7 (PDF p. 12). Furthermore, on the secondary water-source location outcome (Homesource, Table 4, PDF pp. 12-13, N = 44,546), regional utilities corruption is null (-0.26, SE = 0.202) whereas individual household bribery is positively associated with having a source inside the house or compound (+0.06***, SE = 0.018; individual bribery is null on Access in Table 2 Col 3 at -0.00, SE = 0.006, though positive in leave-one-out Table A5 per Endnote 5, PDF p. 14). Finally, Family C fit is borderline because the exposure is an empirical regional bribery prevalence proxy pooled across water, sanitation, and electricity services jointly (PDF p. 8) rather than a water-specific legal or regulatory rule, and any synthesis harmonizing governance exposures positively (anti-corruption integrity -> access) must invert 'Unfavourable' to 'Favourable'.

numerical_check_note: Claude's stored sample size (N = 44,778 in Table 1, Table 2 Cols 1 & 3, and Table 3) and narrative magnitudes ('10% less likely' across the 0 to 0.708 corruption range and '0.5% drop' per 1-SD [0.0422] increase, PDF p. 10, where the authors conflate percentage points with %) match the paper's prose verbatim. However, Claude failed to extract the exact printed probit marginal effects and standard errors in Table 2 (Col 2 without own bribery: -0.15**, SE = 0.073, N = 44,887; Col 3 with own bribery: -0.16**, SE = 0.073, N = 44,778; Col 5 with other corruption: -0.13*, SE = 0.073, N = 44,887; Col 6 non-piped: -0.12, SE = 0.158, N = 20,267; Col 7 piped: -0.14***, SE = 0.045, N = 24,511) and Table 3 ('Never': -0.4272**, SE = 0.1860; 'Always': +0.1095**, SE = 0.0481), erroneously logging numeric SEs as unavailable ('none, none / clustered by region'), and omitted 'Poverty index' (lived poverty index, -0.01***, SE = 0.001) from the stored covariate list. Note also that the dossier's automated number-matcher matched '10%' to an unrelated Transparency International quote on PDF p. 3 rather than PDF p. 10.
polarity_or_orientation_issue: Step-by-step trace holds as coded but contains two synthesis traps: (1) Exposure orientation: 'Regional incidence of utility corruption' is scaled 0 to 1 where higher = MORE bribery/worse governance ('as reported'); combined with binary Access = 1 if anything other than 'always' lacking clean water ('higher = better', mean = 0.907), the negative raw marginal effect (-0.16**) means corruption is 'Unfavourable' to access. If Family C syntheses orient institutional governance exposures positively (control of corruption / regulatory integrity), the direction flips to 'Favourable'. (2) Outcome polarity flip between Table 2 and Table 3: Claude cites Table 3 (ordered probit) alongside Table 2 under raw sign '-', which is true for the 'Never' shortage category (-0.4272**), whereas the remaining four Table 3 columns ('Just once or twice' through 'Always' going without water) measure shortage frequency ('higher = worse') and therefore carry positive raw signs (+0.0324** to +0.1095**) denoting the same unfavourable substantive effect.
